1319	// handleSessionPostChanges is the session-scoped batch commit over the same
1320	// change collection the session reads page:
1321	//
1322	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes
1323	//
1324	// The request body carries only the changes array — the calling device is the
1325	// session's owning device, resolved with the same identity rule as the
1326	// session reads, exports and subscriptions; no new credential is introduced
1327	// and no device id travels in the body. Per-element semantics and the success
1328	// body are byte-identical to the document-level commit: results arrive in
1329	// request order, each naming its id, whether it was created and the cursor it
1330	// was assigned. The checks run in the fixed order request shape (400),
1331	// session existence (404), document permission (403) — the permission verdict
1332	// is taken inside the commit transaction, so a revoked device writes nothing —
1333	// and a payload/device mismatch against an existing id is a 409 reporting the
1334	// conflicting id. Every rejection leaves the log untouched.
1335	func handleSessionPostChanges(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1336		sessionID := r.PathValue("sessionId")   // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1337		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1338	
1339		var req sessionPostRequest
1340		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
1341			return
1342		}
1343		if len(req.Changes) == 0 {
1344			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "changes must be a non-empty array")
1345			return
1346		}
1347	
1348		changes := make([]events.Change, len(req.Changes))
1349		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(req.Changes))
1350		for i, c := range req.Changes {
1351			if c.ID == "" {
1352				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each change must have a non-empty string id")
1353				return
1354			}
1355			if len(c.Payload) == 0 {
1356				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each change must carry a JSON payload")
1357				return
1358			}
1359			if _, dup := seen[c.ID]; dup {
1360				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "duplicate change id within batch: "+c.ID)
1361				return
1362			}
1363			seen[c.ID] = struct{}{}
1364			changes[i] = events.Change{ID: c.ID, Payload: c.Payload}
1365		}

1367		// Request shape is settled; only now does the session lookup run, so a
1368		// malformed batch against an unknown session is still a 400.

1371			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {

1374			}
1375			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
1376			return
1377		}

1389				// identity the caller used no longer exists.

1391			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrPermissionDenied):
1392				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
1393			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
1394				writeJSON(w, http.StatusConflict, map[string]string{
1395					"error":      "change id already exists with different deviceId or payload",
1396					"conflictId": conflict.ID,
1397				})
1398			default:
1399				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to commit changes")
1400			}
1401			return
1402		}

1	// Package app is the composition root: it opens the one shared database and
2	// constructs the three independently reusable internal services — the change
3	// event service, the permission service and the CRDT state service — wiring
4	// them together only through their internal interfaces.
5	//
6	// The services share one SQLite connection (the kernel opens a single
7	// pooled connection with immediate transactions), so a change commit, a CRDT
8	// submission or compaction, and a permission change are serialized on the
9	// same connection and leave no half-written batch. The change event and CRDT
10	// services take their registration-and-authorization verdict from the
11	// permission service inside their own transactions (events.Gate / crdt.Gate),
12	// and the permission service fans a committed revoke out to their
13	// subscription registries through authz.RevokeSink. No service reaches into
14	// another service's tables or fields.
15	//
16	// App is the single object the entry and HTTP layers use. It promotes each
17	// service's input/output boundary as its methods while hiding the wiring; it
18	// adds no authentication and exposes no endpoint of its own.
19	package app
20	
21	import (
22		"context"
23		"encoding/json"
24		"time"
25	
26		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/authz"
27		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/crdt"
28		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/events"
29		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/push"
30		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
31	)
32	
33	// App composes the durable kernel and the three internal services over one
34	// shared database connection.
35	type App struct {
36		*store.Store
37	
38		events *events.Service
39		crdt   *crdt.Service
40	
41		// pushSubs is the process-wide, in-memory registry of the live push
42		// connections across both channels. It backs the device-scoped
43		// subscription management endpoints and holds no durable state.
44		pushSubs *push.Registry
45	
46		// Authz is the permission service. It is exposed so the HTTP layer can
47		// grant/revoke and read authorization directly; the other services reach
48		// it through their gates rather than this field.
49		Authz *authz.Service
50	}
51	
52	// Open opens (creating if needed) the SQLite database at path and constructs
53	// every internal service over it. The empty path opens a private in-memory
54	// database useful for tests. A construction failure closes the kernel and
55	// leaves nothing behind.
56	func Open(path string) (*App, error) {
57		kernel, err := store.Open(path)
58		if err != nil {
59			return nil, err
60		}
61	
62		// The permission service is built first: its gate is a constructor
63		// dependency of the change event and CRDT services.
64		permissions, err := authz.New(kernel)
65		if err != nil {
66			_ = kernel.Close()
67			return nil, err
68		}
69		eventService, err := events.New(kernel, permissions)
70		if err != nil {
71			_ = kernel.Close()
72			return nil, err
73		}
74		crdtService, err := crdt.New(kernel, permissions)
75		if err != nil {
76			_ = kernel.Close()
77			return nil, err
78		}
79	
80		// A committed revoke ends the affected live subscriptions in both
81		// push channels. The dependency is an interface, registered once here, so
82		// the permission service never names either subscriber concretely.
83		permissions.AddRevokeSink(eventsRevokeSink{eventService})
84		permissions.AddRevokeSink(crdtService)
85	
86		return &App{
87			Store:    kernel,
88			events:   eventService,
89			crdt:     crdtService,
90			Authz:    permissions,
91			pushSubs: push.NewRegistry(),
92		}, nil
93	}
94	
95	// eventsRevokeSink adapts the change event service's revoke hook to the
96	// permission service's RevokeSink interface.
97	type eventsRevokeSink struct{ e *events.Service }
98	
99	func (s eventsRevokeSink) PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID string) {
100		s.e.SignalRevoked(documentID, deviceID)
101	}
102	
103	// Events returns the change event service.
104	func (a *App) Events() *events.Service { return a.events }
105	
106	// CRDT returns the CRDT state service.
107	func (a *App) CRDT() *crdt.Service { return a.crdt }
108	
109	// ---- Change event service boundary (promoted so the entry layer has one
110	// object; each method delegates verbatim to the events service). ----
111	
112	// InterruptWaits wakes every parked long poll and every live change-log and
113	// CRDT subscription without closing the database, so an orderly shutdown
114	// drains waiting connections (long polls answer 503; subscriptions finish
115	// with the going-away close) instead of holding the drain hostage.
116	func (a *App) InterruptWaits() {
117		a.events.InterruptWaits()
118		a.crdt.InterruptWaits()
119	}
120	
121	// Closing reports whether shutdown has begun, covering both push channels.
122	func (a *App) Closing() bool {
123		return a.events.Closing() || a.crdt.Closing()
124	}
125	
126	// Close interrupts the in-memory observers, waits for every subscription
127	// handler to unregister and then releases the shared database handle.
128	func (a *App) Close() error {
129		a.events.InterruptWaits()
130		a.crdt.InterruptWaits()
131		a.events.WaitDrained()
132		a.crdt.WaitDrained()
133		return a.Store.Close()
134	}
135	
136	// PostChanges delegates to the change event service.
137	func (a *App) PostChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
138		return a.events.PostChanges(documentID, changes)
139	}
140	
141	// ReplayChanges delegates to the change event service.
142	func (a *App) ReplayChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
143		return a.events.ReplayChanges(documentID, changes)
144	}
145	
146	// PostSessionChanges commits a batch whose device identity was resolved from
147	// a session by the HTTP layer, delegating to the change event service's
148	// gated commit: the registration/permission verdict is taken inside the same
149	// serialized transaction as the write, so a revoked device commits nothing.
150	func (a *App) PostSessionChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
151		return a.events.CommitAuthorized(documentID, changes)
152	}
153	
154	// ReplaySessionChanges replays an offline batch whose device identity was
155	// resolved from a session by the HTTP layer; it is the session counterpart

1	// Package store is the durable kernel shared by the internal services: it
2	// owns the SQLite database handle and the registration layer (devices and
3	// sessions) plus resumable attachments.
4	//
5	// The business services layered on top of the kernel — the change event log,
6	// the permission ledger and the CRDT state — live in their own packages and
7	// cooperate only through their internal interfaces. They all share this one
8	// handle: it opens a single pooled connection with immediate write
9	// transactions, so every service's transactional judgment is serialized on
10	// the same connection and no batch is ever half written.
11	//
12	// Devices and sessions form the registration layer. A device registers with a
13	// client-supplied id; a session belongs to exactly one registered device and
14	// is addressed by its own client-supplied id. Registration and session
15	// creation are idempotent re-posts: the first call creates, an identical
16	// repeat does not. A session id already owned by another device is a
17	// conflict, never silently re-homed. Deletes are owner-scoped and hard: a
18	// repeat delete, another device, and a cross-device path all miss with 404,
19	// after which the id is free to be created again. A device itself can
20	// deregister: the device row and everything it owns — its sessions and the
21	// attachments it created, chunks and grants included — vanish in one
22	// serialized transaction, a repeat or never-registered deregistration misses
23	// with 404 and writes nothing, and the freed id registers again as a
24	// brand-new device.
25	//
26	// Attachments are resumable chunked uploads owned by the registered device
27	// that created them. Creation pins the declared total size, chunk size and
28	// SHA-256 digest; chunks land in any order and are stored durably as they
29	// arrive, so an interrupted upload resumes after a restart with its
30	// idempotency and conflict decisions intact. Finishing concatenates the
31	// chunks, verifies the digest and seals the upload; a sealed upload is
32	// immutable and rejects every further chunk write. Finished content is
33	// addressed by digest, so a second attachment with the same digest and size
34	// reuses the stored bytes instead of copying them. The creator may grant
35	// other registered devices read-only access per attachment; every
36	// (attachment, device) pair starts unauthorized, grants and revokes commit in
37	// the same serialized way, and access never widens the write paths. Deletes
38	// are owner-scoped and hard: the record, its chunks and its grants vanish in
39	// one serialized transaction, a repeat delete misses with 404, the id is free
40	// to be created again, and the shared content bytes are reclaimed once the
41	// last completed attachment referencing them is gone.
42	package store
43	
44	import (
45		"database/sql"
46		"encoding/json"
47		"errors"
48		"fmt"
49	
50		_ "modernc.org/sqlite"
51	)
52	
53	// ErrDeviceNotFound reports that an operation targets a device id that was
54	// never registered. Services map it to 404; nothing is written.
55	var ErrDeviceNotFound = errors.New("device not found")
56	
57	// ErrPermissionDenied reports that a device's access to a document has been
58	// revoked. Services map it to 403; nothing is written and no document content
59	// is exposed. It is a shared verdict produced by the permission service and
60	// consulted by every service that enforces the gate inside a transaction.
61	var ErrPermissionDenied = errors.New("device permission for this document has been revoked")
62	
63	// ErrSessionConflict reports that a session id already belongs to a different
64	// device. The session keeps its original owner; nothing is written. Services
65	// map it to 409.
66	type ErrSessionConflict struct {
67		ID string
68	}
69	
70	func (e *ErrSessionConflict) Error() string {
71		return fmt.Sprintf("session %q belongs to another device", e.ID)
72	}
73	
74	// ErrSessionNotFound reports that no live session matches the (device,
75	// session) pair: the session was never created, was already deleted, or
76	// belongs to another device. Services map it to 404.
77	var ErrSessionNotFound = errors.New("session not found")
78	
79	// DBTX is the subset of *sql.DB and *sql.Tx the services use for their
80	// serialized work, so judgments made "in the same transaction" (for example a
81	// permission gate followed by the gated write) run on one concrete connection
82	// whether the caller holds a transaction or the handle itself.
83	type DBTX interface {
84		Exec(query string, args ...any) (sql.Result, error)
85		Query(query string, args ...any) (*sql.Rows, error)
86		QueryRow(query string, args ...any) *sql.Row
87	}
88	
89	// Store is the durable kernel: one SQLite database handle together with the
90	// device, session and attachment data it owns.
91	type Store struct {
92		db *sql.DB
93	}
94	
95	// Open opens (creating if needed) the SQLite database at path. The empty path
96	// opens an in-memory database useful for tests.
97	func Open(path string) (*Store, error) {
98		if path == "" {
99			// With a single pooled connection this is a private, per-instance
100			// in-memory database (useful for tests).
101			path = "file::memory:"
102		}
103		// _txlock=immediate makes writers acquire the write lock at BEGIN, so
104		// concurrent batches serialize without SQLITE_BUSY deadlocks.
105		dsn := path + "?_txlock=immediate&_busy_timeout=5000&_journal_mode=WAL&_synchronous=FULL&_foreign_keys=on"
106		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", dsn)
107		if err != nil {
108			return nil, err
109		}
110		// One connection avoids cross-connection locking surprises; writes are
111		// serialized by the immediate transaction anyway, and SQLite concurrency
112		// for readers does not help correctness here. It also keeps every
113		// service's transaction serialized on the same connection.
114		db.SetMaxOpenConns(1)
115		s := &Store{db: db}
116		if err := s.init(); err != nil {
117			_ = db.Close()
118			return nil, err
119		}
120		return s, nil
121	}
122	
123	// DB returns the underlying handle. The business services use it to open the
124	// serialized transactions their judgments run in; callers outside the
125	// internal packages never need it.
126	func (s *Store) DB() *sql.DB { return s.db }
127	
128	// Close releases the database handle.
129	func (s *Store) Close() error {
130		return s.db.Close()
131	}
132	
133	func (s *Store) init() error {
134		_, err := s.db.Exec(`
135	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS devices (
136		id TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY
137	);
138	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
139		id        TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
140		device_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(id)
141	);
142	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS sessions_device_idx
143		ON sessions(device_id);
144	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attachments (
145		id          TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
146		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(id),
147		total_bytes INTEGER NOT NULL,
148		chunk_size  INTEGER NOT NULL,
149		sha256      TEXT NOT NULL,
150		complete    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
151		reused      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
152		created_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
153	);
154	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attachment_chunks (
155		attachment_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES attachments(id),
156		idx           INTEGER NOT NULL,
157		data          BLOB NOT NULL,
158		PRIMARY KEY (attachment_id, idx)
159	);
160	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attachment_contents (
161		sha256 TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
162		size   INTEGER NOT NULL,
163		data   BLOB NOT NULL
164	);
165	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attachment_access (
166		attachment_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES attachments(id),
167		device_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
168		authorized    INTEGER NOT NULL,
169		granted_seq   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
170		PRIMARY KEY (attachment_id, device_id)
171	);
172	`)
173		if err != nil {
174			return err
175		}
176		if err := s.ensureAttachmentCreatedSeq(); err != nil {
177			return err
178		}
179		return s.ensureAttachmentAccessGrantedSeq()
180	}
181	
182	// ensureAttachmentCreatedSeq adds the creation-order column to databases
183	// created before it existed. Existing rows are backfilled in insertion
184	// (rowid) order so their relative listing order is unchanged; new rows take
185	// strictly larger values, so the sequence never reuses a value even after
186	// the newest attachment is deleted and its id created again.
187	func (s *Store) ensureAttachmentCreatedSeq() error {
188		rows, err := s.db.Query(`PRAGMA table_info(attachments)`)
189		if err != nil {
190			return err
191		}
192		hasColumn := false
193		for rows.Next() {
194			var cid, notNull, pk int
195			var name, colType string
196			var dflt sql.NullString
197			if err := rows.Scan(&cid, &name, &colType, &notNull, &dflt, &pk); err != nil {
198				_ = rows.Close()
199				return err
200			}
201			if name == "created_seq" {
202				hasColumn = true
203			}
204		}
205		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
206			_ = rows.Close()
207			return err
208		}
209		_ = rows.Close()
210		if hasColumn {
211			return nil
212		}
213		if _, err := s.db.Exec(
214			`ALTER TABLE attachments ADD COLUMN created_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`,
215		); err != nil {
216			return err
217		}
218		_, err = s.db.Exec(
219			`UPDATE attachments SET created_seq = (
220				SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attachments older WHERE older.rowid <= attachments.rowid
221			)`,
222		)
223		return err
224	}
225	
226	// ensureAttachmentAccessGrantedSeq adds the grant-order column to access
227	// tables created before it existed. Existing rows are backfilled one past the
228	// per-attachment maximum in insertion (rowid) order, so surviving grants keep
229	// a stable relative order; every new grant takes a strictly larger value, even
230	// after the previously newest grant was revoked, so a re-granted device lists
231	// at the position of its latest grant and a value is never reused.
232	func (s *Store) ensureAttachmentAccessGrantedSeq() error {
233		rows, err := s.db.Query(`PRAGMA table_info(attachment_access)`)
234		if err != nil {
235			return err
236		}
237		hasColumn := false
238		for rows.Next() {
239			var cid, notNull, pk int
240			var name, colType string
241			var dflt sql.NullString
242			if err := rows.Scan(&cid, &name, &colType, &notNull, &dflt, &pk); err != nil {
243				_ = rows.Close()
244				return err
245			}
246			if name == "granted_seq" {
247				hasColumn = true
248			}
249		}
250		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
251			_ = rows.Close()
252			return err
253		}
254		_ = rows.Close()
255		if hasColumn {
256			return nil
257		}
258		if _, err := s.db.Exec(
259			`ALTER TABLE attachment_access ADD COLUMN granted_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`,
260		); err != nil {
261			return err
262		}
263		_, err = s.db.Exec(
264			`UPDATE attachment_access SET granted_seq = (
265				SELECT rn FROM (
266					SELECT rowid AS rid,
267					       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY attachment_id ORDER BY rowid) AS rn
268					FROM attachment_access
269				) WHERE rid = attachment_access.rowid
270			)`,
271		)
272		return err
273	}
274	
275	// RegisterDevice registers a device by client-supplied id. The first call for
276	// an id creates it and reports created=true; repeating the registration is
277	// idempotent (created=false). Device identity never changes.
278	func (s *Store) RegisterDevice(deviceID string) (created bool, err error) {
279		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
280		if err != nil {
281			return false, err
282		}
283		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
284	
285		created, err = RegisterDeviceTx(tx, deviceID)
286		if err != nil {
287			return false, err
288		}
289		return created, tx.Commit()
290	}
291	
292	// RegisterDeviceTx is RegisterDevice against an existing transaction, so the
293	// services can resolve the registration layer as the first step of a larger
294	// serialized transaction (their permission/content gates then share it).
295	func RegisterDeviceTx(q DBTX, deviceID string) (created bool, err error) {
296		var exists bool
297		if err := q.QueryRow(
298			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
299		).Scan(&exists); err != nil {
300			return false, err
301		}
302		if !exists {
303			if _, err := q.Exec(`INSERT INTO devices (id) VALUES (?)`, deviceID); err != nil {
304				return false, err
305			}
306			return true, nil
307		}
308		return false, nil
309	}
310	
311	// DeviceExistsTx reports whether deviceID is registered, evaluated inside q so
312	// a service's gate runs on the same transaction as the work it guards.
313	func DeviceExistsTx(q DBTX, deviceID string) (bool, error) {
314		var exists bool
315		if err := q.QueryRow(
316			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
317		).Scan(&exists); err != nil {
318			return false, err
319		}
320		return exists, nil
321	}
322	
323	// CreateSession creates a session owned by deviceID with a client-supplied id.
324	//
325	//   - An unknown device yields ErrDeviceNotFound; nothing is written.
326	//   - A session id already owned by another device yields *ErrSessionConflict;
327	//     nothing is written and the owner is unchanged.
328	//   - Re-posting the same (device, session) pair is idempotent: created=false.
329	//
330	// A deleted session is gone for good, so its id can be registered again as a
331	// brand-new session (created=true). The lookup, owner check and insert run in
332	// one serialized transaction, so concurrent creates of the same session id
333	// cannot both create it.
334	func (s *Store) CreateSession(deviceID, sessionID string) (created bool, err error) {
335		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
336		if err != nil {
337			return false, err
338		}
339		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
340	
341		var deviceExists bool
342		if err := tx.QueryRow(
343			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
344		).Scan(&deviceExists); err != nil {
345			return false, err
346		}
347		if !deviceExists {
348			return false, ErrDeviceNotFound
349		}
350	
351		var owner string
352		err = tx.QueryRow(
353			`SELECT device_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?`, sessionID,
354		).Scan(&owner)
355		switch {
356		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
357			if _, err := tx.Exec(
358				`INSERT INTO sessions (id, device_id) VALUES (?, ?)`,
359				sessionID, deviceID,
360			); err != nil {
361				return false, err
362			}
363			if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
364				return false, err
365			}
366			return true, nil
367		case err != nil:
368			return false, err
369		}
370	
371		if owner != deviceID {
372			return false, &ErrSessionConflict{ID: sessionID}
373		}
374		return false, tx.Commit()
375	}
376	
377	// DeleteSession removes the live session matching the (deviceID, sessionID)
378	// pair. Any miss — the session does not exist, was already deleted, or belongs
379	// to another device — returns ErrSessionNotFound and changes nothing. The
380	// check and the delete run in one transaction, so a concurrent create cannot
381	// interleave and a repeat delete still misses; the removal is committed to
382	// disk before the call returns.
383	func (s *Store) DeleteSession(deviceID, sessionID string) error {
384		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
385		if err != nil {
386			return err
387		}
388		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
389	
390		var owner string
391		err = tx.QueryRow(
392			`SELECT device_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?`, sessionID,
393		).Scan(&owner)
394		switch {
395		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
396			return ErrSessionNotFound
397		case err != nil:
398			return err
399		}
400		if owner != deviceID {
401			return ErrSessionNotFound
402		}
403	
404		if _, err := tx.Exec(
405			`DELETE FROM sessions WHERE id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
406			sessionID, deviceID,
407		); err != nil {
408			return err
409		}
410		return tx.Commit()
411	}
412	
413	// DeleteDeviceTx deregisters deviceID and removes every record it owns, all
414	// inside the caller's serialized transaction:
415	//
416	//   - the device's sessions are hard-deleted, so their session-scoped reads
417	//     and subscriptions miss from then on;
418	//   - every attachment it created is removed together with its chunks, its
419	//     sealed/unfinished state and the access rows other devices held on it;
420	//   - the read grants the device itself held on other devices' attachments
421	//     are withdrawn;
422	//   - the device row is removed last (every child row goes first).
423	//
424	// Digest-addressed content is shared across attachments and is reclaimed only
425	// when no completed attachment still references a digest — exactly the rule
426	// of a single attachment delete — so another device's attachment with the same
427	// digest keeps its bytes and one deregistration by itself never reclaims
428	// shared content. The document permission ledger lives in the authz package
429	// and clears its own rows against the same transaction through
430	// DeleteDevicePermissionsTx.
431	//
432	// An unknown (never registered or already deregistered) device yields
433	// ErrDeviceNotFound and writes nothing. Because the whole judgment runs in one
434	// immediate transaction on the single shared connection, concurrent
435	// deregistrations of the same device commit at most once and any concurrent
436	// chunk upload or finish either committed entirely before it or is rejected
437	// entirely afterward — no half-written record survives.
438	func DeleteDeviceTx(q DBTX, deviceID string) error {
439		exists, err := DeviceExistsTx(q, deviceID)
440		if err != nil {
441			return err
442		}
443		if !exists {
444			return ErrDeviceNotFound
445		}
446	
447		// Remember the digests of the device's completed attachments before their
448		// rows vanish: each is a candidate for content reclamation once every
449		// owned attachment is gone. DISTINCT because several of the device's
450		// attachments may share the same digest-addressed content.
451		rows, err := q.Query(
452			`SELECT DISTINCT sha256 FROM attachments WHERE device_id = ? AND complete = 1`,
453			deviceID,
454		)
455		if err != nil {
456			return err
457		}
458		var digests []string
459		for rows.Next() {
460			var digest string
461			if err := rows.Scan(&digest); err != nil {
462				_ = rows.Close()
463				return err
464			}
465			digests = append(digests, digest)
466		}
467		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
468			_ = rows.Close()
469			return err
470		}
471		if err := rows.Close(); err != nil {
472			return err
473		}
474	
475		// Withdraw the read grants this device held on other devices'
476		// attachments (rows naming it as the grantee), then remove the access
477		// rosters of the attachments it created before the attachment rows those
478		// rosters reference are deleted.
479		if _, err := q.Exec(
480			`DELETE FROM attachment_access WHERE device_id = ?`, deviceID,
481		); err != nil {
482			return err
483		}
484		if _, err := q.Exec(
485			`DELETE FROM attachment_access
486			 WHERE attachment_id IN (SELECT id FROM attachments WHERE device_id = ?)`,
487			deviceID,
488		); err != nil {
489			return err
490		}
491		if _, err := q.Exec(
492			`DELETE FROM attachment_chunks
493			 WHERE attachment_id IN (SELECT id FROM attachments WHERE device_id = ?)`,
494			deviceID,
495		); err != nil {
496			return err
497		}
498		if _, err := q.Exec(
499			`DELETE FROM attachments WHERE device_id = ?`, deviceID,
500		); err != nil {
501			return err
502		}
503	
504		// Reclaim each digest-addressed content only when no surviving completed
505		// attachment — owned by another device, or by the deregistered device in
506		// an impossible re-read — still references it.
507		for _, digest := range digests {
508			var stillReferenced bool
509			if err := q.QueryRow(
510				`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM attachments WHERE sha256 = ? AND complete = 1)`,
511				digest,
512			).Scan(&stillReferenced); err != nil {
513				return err
514			}
515			if !stillReferenced {
516				if _, err := q.Exec(
517					`DELETE FROM attachment_contents WHERE sha256 = ?`, digest,
518				); err != nil {
519					return err
520				}
521			}
522		}
523	
524		if _, err := q.Exec(
525			`DELETE FROM sessions WHERE device_id = ?`, deviceID,
526		); err != nil {
527			return err
528		}
529		if _, err := q.Exec(
530			`DELETE FROM devices WHERE id = ?`, deviceID,
531		); err != nil {
532			return err
533		}
534		return nil
535	}
536	
537	// DeviceExists reports whether a live device with deviceID is registered. It
538	// is the non-transactional counterpart to DeviceExistsTx, used by the
539	// document-level subscription handlers whose existence verdict runs before
540	// the WebSocket upgrade rather than inside a write transaction.
541	func (s *Store) DeviceExists(deviceID string) (bool, error) {
542		return DeviceExistsTx(s.db, deviceID)
543	}
544	
545	// SessionExists reports whether a live session with sessionID exists.
546	// Ownership is intentionally not part of this check: session-scoped reads only
547	// require that the session currently exists.
548	func (s *Store) SessionExists(sessionID string) (bool, error) {
549		var exists bool
550		if err := s.db.QueryRow(
551			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sessions WHERE id = ?)`, sessionID,
552		).Scan(&exists); err != nil {
553			return false, err
554		}
555		return exists, nil
556	}
557	
558	// SessionDevice returns the id of the device that owns the live session
559	// sessionID. A session that was never created or was deleted yields
560	// ErrSessionNotFound.
561	func (s *Store) SessionDevice(sessionID string) (string, error) {
562		var deviceID string
563		err := s.db.QueryRow(
564			`SELECT device_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?`, sessionID,
565		).Scan(&deviceID)
566		switch {
567		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
568			return "", ErrSessionNotFound
569		case err != nil:
570			return "", err
571		default:
572			return deviceID, nil
573		}
574	}
575	
576	// JSONEqual reports whether two payloads are equal after JSON decoding, so
577	// 1 and 1.0, or {"a":1,"b":2} and {"b":2,"a":1}, compare equal. It is shared
578	// verbatim by the change event and CRDT services' idempotency judgments.
579	func JSONEqual(a, b json.RawMessage) bool {
580		var va, vb any
581		if err := json.Unmarshal(a, &va); err != nil {
582			return false
583		}
584		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &vb); err != nil {
585			return false
586		}
587		return deepEqual(va, vb)
588	}
589	
590	func deepEqual(a, b any) bool {
591		switch av := a.(type) {
592		case nil:
593			return b == nil
594		case bool:
595			bv, ok := b.(bool)
596			return ok && av == bv
597		case string:
598			bv, ok := b.(string)
599			return ok && av == bv
600		case float64:
601			bv, ok := b.(float64)
602			return ok && av == bv
603		case []any:
604			bv, ok := b.([]any)
605			if !ok || len(av) != len(bv) {
606				return false
607			}
608			for i := range av {
609				if !deepEqual(av[i], bv[i]) {
610					return false
611				}
612			}
613			return true
614		case map[string]any:
615			bv, ok := b.(map[string]any)
616			if !ok || len(av) != len(bv) {
617				return false
618			}
619			for k, v := range av {
620				w, exists := bv[k]
621				if !exists || !deepEqual(v, w) {
622					return false
623				}
624			}
625			return true
626		default:
627			return false
628		}
629	}

1	// Change-log compaction moves the old end of a document's change log out of
2	// the online tables without touching the cursor space the log shares with
3	// every write path.
4	//
5	// The compaction boundary is the greatest cursor that has a saved snapshot
6	// (zero when the document has none): everything at or below it is reproducible
7	// from a snapshot plus the surviving tail, so those rows leave the online log.
8	// A trimmed change is not forgotten, though — its id keeps a small canonical
9	// summary (the originating device, a digest of the payload and, for a restore,
10	// the snapshot it came from, plus the cursor it was first assigned) so the
11	// submission layer keeps answering idempotency and conflict exactly as before.
12	// The summary never participates in reads: pagination, long polling and
13	// subscriptions simply no longer see the trimmed rows, and the summary's
14	// fixed size means storage does not grow back to the pre-compaction shape.
15	//
16	// Compaction itself is not a change: it allocates no cursor, writes no change
17	// record and wakes no waiter or subscriber. The cursor space never resets —
18	// the next allocated cursor is one past the greater of the online maximum and
19	// the boundary — and the boundary, the summaries and the read results are
20	// durable across restarts.
21	
22	package events
23	
24	import (
25		"bytes"
26		"crypto/sha256"
27		"database/sql"
28		"encoding/json"
29		"errors"
30	
31		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
32	)
33	
34	// CompactChanges moves every change of documentID whose cursor is at or below
35	// the compaction boundary out of the online log, in one serialized
36	// transaction, and returns the boundary together with the number of changes
37	// removed by this call.
38	//
39	// The boundary is the greatest cursor with a saved snapshot, or zero when the
40	// document has no snapshot — compacting a snapshot-less or unknown document
41	// succeeds and removes nothing. The gate is enforced before any content is
42	// observed, exactly as in ReplayChanges: an unregistered device yields
43	// store.ErrDeviceNotFound and a revoked device yields store.ErrPermissionDenied,
44	// and neither touches any state.
45	//
46	// Each trimmed id keeps its canonical summary (device, payload digest, restore
47	// provenance and first cursor) so re-posting it stays idempotent and a
48	// differing re-post stays a conflict. Compaction is idempotent: a repeat finds
49	// the same boundary, trims nothing and reports zero removed. It commits no
50	// change row, allocates no cursor and notifies no waiter or subscriber.
51	func (s *Service) CompactChanges(documentID, deviceID string) (boundary, removed int64, err error) {
52		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
53		if err != nil {
54			return 0, 0, err
55		}
56		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
57	
58		// Registration and permission are enforced before any change content is
59		// observed, so a rejected compaction cannot reveal anything.
60		if s.gate != nil {
61			if err := s.gate.DeviceAuthorizedTx(tx, documentID, deviceID); err != nil {
62				return 0, 0, err
63			}
64		}
65	
66		// The boundary is the greatest cursor with a saved snapshot, 0 when the
67		// document has none (an unknown document included).
68		if err := tx.QueryRow(
69			`SELECT COALESCE(MAX(cursor), 0) FROM snapshots WHERE document_id = ?`,
70			documentID,
71		).Scan(&boundary); err != nil {
72			return 0, 0, err
73		}
74		stored, err := boundaryOfTx(tx, documentID)
75		if err != nil {
76			return 0, 0, err
77		}
78		if boundary <= stored {
79			// Nothing new to trim (a repeat compaction, or a snapshot-less
80			// document): report the standing boundary and remove nothing.
81			return stored, 0, tx.Commit()
82		}
83	
84		// Collect the rows leaving the online log before deleting them: each one
85		// first moves its canonical summary into the identity table.
86		type trimmed struct {
87			cursor  int64
88			id      string
89			device  string
90			payload []byte
91		}
92		rows, err := tx.Query(
93			`SELECT cursor, id, device_id, payload FROM changes
94			 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor <= ?
95			 ORDER BY cursor ASC`,
96			documentID, boundary,
97		)
98		if err != nil {
99			return 0, 0, err
100		}
101		var dropping []trimmed
102		for rows.Next() {
103			var t trimmed
104			if err := rows.Scan(&t.cursor, &t.id, &t.device, &t.payload); err != nil {
105				_ = rows.Close()
106				return 0, 0, err
107			}
108			dropping = append(dropping, t)
109		}
110		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
111			_ = rows.Close()
112			return 0, 0, err
113		}
114		_ = rows.Close()
115	
116		for _, t := range dropping {
117			// A restored change also carries its provenance into the summary, so a
118			// repeated restore keeps its idempotency/conflict decision.
119			var restoredFrom sql.NullInt64
120			err := tx.QueryRow(
121				`SELECT snapshot_cursor FROM restores WHERE document_id = ? AND change_id = ?`,
122				documentID, t.id,
123			).Scan(&restoredFrom)
124			switch {
125			case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
126				restoredFrom = sql.NullInt64{}
127			case err != nil:
128				return 0, 0, err
129			}
130			digest, err := payloadDigest(t.payload)
131			if err != nil {
132				return 0, 0, err
133			}
134			if _, err := tx.Exec(
135				`INSERT OR IGNORE INTO change_identities
136					(document_id, id, device_id, digest, cursor, restored_from)
137				 VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
138				documentID, t.id, t.device, digest, t.cursor, restoredFrom,
139			); err != nil {
140				return 0, 0, err
141			}
142		}
143	
144		if _, err := tx.Exec(
145			`DELETE FROM restores WHERE document_id = ? AND change_cursor <= ?`,
146			documentID, boundary,
147		); err != nil {
148			return 0, 0, err
149		}
150		if _, err := tx.Exec(
151			`DELETE FROM changes WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor <= ?`,
152			documentID, boundary,
153		); err != nil {
154			return 0, 0, err
155		}
156		if _, err := tx.Exec(
157			`INSERT INTO change_boundaries (document_id, boundary) VALUES (?, ?)
158			 ON CONFLICT (document_id) DO UPDATE SET boundary = excluded.boundary`,
159			documentID, boundary,
160		); err != nil {
161			return 0, 0, err
162		}
163	
164		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
165			return 0, 0, err
166		}
167		// Compaction is not a change: no waiter is woken and no subscriber is
168		// signaled, because no new change exists to observe.
169		return boundary, int64(len(dropping)), nil
170	}
171	
172	// boundaryOfTx returns the stored compaction boundary of documentID, or zero
173	// when the document was never compacted.
174	func boundaryOfTx(q store.DBTX, documentID string) (int64, error) {
175		var boundary int64
176		err := q.QueryRow(
177			`SELECT boundary FROM change_boundaries WHERE document_id = ?`,
178			documentID,
179		).Scan(&boundary)
180		switch {
181		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
182			return 0, nil
183		case err != nil:
184			return 0, err
185		default:
186			return boundary, nil
187		}
188	}
189	
190	// currentCursorTx returns the document's high-water mark: the greatest online
191	// cursor, or the compaction boundary when every change up to it has left the
192	// online log. The cursor space never resets, so a fully trimmed document
193	// continues from its boundary rather than from zero.
194	func currentCursorTx(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string) (int64, error) {
195		var maxOnline int64
196		if err := tx.QueryRow(
197			`SELECT COALESCE(MAX(cursor), 0) FROM changes WHERE document_id = ?`,
198			documentID,
199		).Scan(&maxOnline); err != nil {
200			return 0, err
201		}
202		boundary, err := boundaryOfTx(tx, documentID)
203		if err != nil {
204			return 0, err
205		}
206		if boundary > maxOnline {
207			maxOnline = boundary
208		}
209		return maxOnline, nil
210	}
211	
212	// payloadDigest renders a payload in the canonical form JSONEqual compares —
213	// the decoded value re-encoded, so 1 and 1.0 or reordered object keys digest
214	// alike — and hashes it. The digest is the fixed-size stand-in for the payload
215	// in a trimmed change's retained summary.
216	func payloadDigest(payload json.RawMessage) ([]byte, error) {
217		var v any
218		if err := json.Unmarshal(payload, &v); err != nil {
219			return nil, err
220		}
221		canonical, err := json.Marshal(v)
222		if err != nil {
223			return nil, err
224		}
225		sum := sha256.Sum256(canonical)
226		return sum[:], nil
227	}
228	
229	// resolveTrimmedIdentity answers the submission question for an id whose
230	// online row is absent because compaction trimmed it. It returns found=true
231	// and the id's first cursor when the retained summary matches the incoming
232	// device and payload (an idempotent re-post), an *ErrConflict when a retained
233	// summary exists but differs, and found=false when no summary was retained (a
234	// genuinely new id).
235	func resolveTrimmedIdentity(tx *sql.Tx, documentID string, c Change) (found bool, cursor int64, err error) {
236		var device string
237		var digest []byte
238		err = tx.QueryRow(
239			`SELECT device_id, digest, cursor FROM change_identities WHERE document_id = ? AND id = ?`,
240			documentID, c.ID,
241		).Scan(&device, &digest, &cursor)
242		switch {
243		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
244			return false, 0, nil
245		case err != nil:
246			return false, 0, err
247		}
248	
249		incoming, err := payloadDigest(c.Payload)
250		if err != nil {
251			return false, 0, err
252		}
253		if device != c.DeviceID || !bytes.Equal(digest, incoming) {
254			return false, 0, &ErrConflict{ID: c.ID}
255		}
256		return true, cursor, nil
257	}

1	package events
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"database/sql"
6		"time"
7	)
8	
9	// DocumentExists reports whether documentID is a known document rather than an
10	// empty namespace: it has any online change row, or a compaction boundary from
11	// a log that was (fully or partially) trimmed.
12	func (s *Service) DocumentExists(documentID string) (bool, error) {
13		var known bool
14		if err := s.db.QueryRow(
15			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM changes WHERE document_id = ?)
16			 OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM change_boundaries WHERE document_id = ?)`,
17			documentID, documentID,
18		).Scan(&known); err != nil {
19			return false, err
20		}
21		return known, nil
22	}
23	
24	// ListChanges returns at most limit changes for documentID whose cursor is
25	// greater than after and still online, in cursor order, together with the
26	// cursor to pass as the next after value. An unknown document yields an empty
27	// list and cursor 0; a known document with no rows past after yields
28	// nextCursor == max(after, boundary), so a caller positioned inside the
29	// trimmed range resumes from the compaction boundary.
30	func (s *Service) ListChanges(documentID string, after, limit int64) ([]ListedChange, int64, error) {
31		rows, err := s.db.Query(
32			`SELECT id, device_id, payload, cursor FROM changes
33			 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor > ?
34			 ORDER BY cursor ASC
35			 LIMIT ?`,
36			documentID, after, limit,
37		)
38		if err != nil {
39			return nil, 0, err
40		}
41		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
42	
43		out := make([]ListedChange, 0)
44		var maxCursor int64 = after
45		for rows.Next() {
46			var c ListedChange
47			if err := rows.Scan(&c.ID, &c.DeviceID, &c.Payload, &c.Cursor); err != nil {
48				return nil, 0, err
49			}
50			out = append(out, c)
51			maxCursor = c.Cursor
52		}
53		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
54			return nil, 0, err
55		}
56	
57		// Distinguish an unknown document from a known one with nothing new:
58		// unknown documents must report nextCursor 0, while a known document
59		// reports the greater of after and the compaction boundary.
60		if len(out) == 0 {
61			known, err := s.DocumentExists(documentID)
62			if err != nil {
63				return nil, 0, err
64			}
65			if !known {
66				return out, 0, nil
67			}
68			boundary, err := boundaryOfTx(s.db, documentID)
69			if err != nil {
70				return nil, 0, err
71			}
72			if boundary > maxCursor {
73				maxCursor = boundary
74			}
75		}
76		return out, maxCursor, nil
77	}
78	
79	// ExportChanges returns every change of documentID whose cursor lies in the
80	// closed interval [from, to] and is still in the online log, in ascending
81	// cursor order. When to is nil no upper bound is applied. An unknown document,
82	// or a range without any online change — including one that lies entirely
83	// inside the trimmed region — yields an empty list and no error: the export is
84	// a read that misses like any other. The (document_id, cursor) unique index
85	// guarantees a cursor appears at most once.
86	//
87	// The single SELECT runs as one SQLite statement over the serialized
88	// connection, so a batch committed concurrently is observed either with all of
89	// its rows or not at all — never half of it. The read starts no transaction,
90	// writes nothing and notifies no waiters, so it cannot move a cursor, produce
91	// a change record or wake a parked poll. Each returned row is the same record
92	// the paged read emits at that cursor.
93	func (s *Service) ExportChanges(documentID string, from int64, to *int64) ([]ListedChange, error) {
94		var (
95			rows *sql.Rows
96			err  error
97		)
98		if to == nil {
99			rows, err = s.db.Query(
100				`SELECT id, device_id, payload, cursor FROM changes
101				 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor >= ?
102				 ORDER BY cursor ASC`,
103				documentID, from,
104			)
105		} else {
106			rows, err = s.db.Query(
107				`SELECT id, device_id, payload, cursor FROM changes
108				 WHERE document_id = ? AND cursor >= ? AND cursor <= ?
109				 ORDER BY cursor ASC`,
110				documentID, from, *to,
111			)
112		}
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, err
115		}
116		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
117	
118		out := make([]ListedChange, 0)
119		for rows.Next() {
120			var c ListedChange
121			if err := rows.Scan(&c.ID, &c.DeviceID, &c.Payload, &c.Cursor); err != nil {
122				return nil, err
123			}
124			out = append(out, c)
125		}
126		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
127			return nil, err
128		}
129		return out, nil
130	}
131	
132	// WaitForChanges blocks until documentID has a change with cursor greater than
133	// after, a change is committed while waiting, wait elapses, ctx is canceled
134	// (the client disconnected) or the service stops. It then returns the current
135	// page of up to limit changes exactly as ListChanges would, with timedOut=true
136	// only when the wait deadline expired with no new rows.
137	//
138	// Registration precedes the first query: a commit landing between the read and
139	// the park still notifies a registered channel, so no change is missed.
140	//
141	// An unknown document is never parked on: it returns immediately with an empty
142	// list and nextCursor 0, timedOut=false. Data already past after is likewise
143	// returned immediately. wait <= 0 is an immediately expired deadline.
144	func (s *Service) WaitForChanges(ctx context.Context, documentID string, after, limit int64, wait time.Duration) (changes []ListedChange, nextCursor int64, timedOut bool, err error) {
145		ch, remove := s.registerWait(documentID)
146		defer remove()
147	
148		changes, nextCursor, err = s.ListChanges(documentID, after, limit)
149		if err != nil || len(changes) > 0 {
150			return changes, nextCursor, false, err
151		}
152	
153		// Empty page: distinguish an unknown document (immediate empty/0, never
154		// parked on) from a known document caught up to after.
155		known, err := s.DocumentExists(documentID)
156		if err != nil || !known {
157			return changes, 0, false, err
158		}
159	
160		// Known document, nothing new: a zero wait is an immediately expired
161		// deadline; ListChanges already echoes nextCursor == after.
162		if wait <= 0 {
163			return changes, nextCursor, true, nil
164		}
165	
166		timer := time.NewTimer(wait)
167		defer timer.Stop()
168	
169		select {
170		case <-ch:
171			// Woken by a committed change or by InterruptWaits.
172			s.mu.Lock()
173			closing := s.closed
174			s.mu.Unlock()
175			if closing {
176				return nil, 0, false, ErrStoreClosing
177			}
178			changes, nextCursor, err = s.ListChanges(documentID, after, limit)
179			return changes, nextCursor, len(changes) == 0, err
180		case <-timer.C:
181			// Timeout with no new rows: echo the caller's cursor without
182			// advancing it. The document was known above, so ListChanges returns
183			// nextCursor == after for an empty page.
184			changes, nextCursor, err = s.ListChanges(documentID, after, limit)
185			return changes, nextCursor, len(changes) == 0, err
186		case <-ctx.Done():
187			return nil, 0, false, ctx.Err()
188		}
189	}
190	
191	// registerWait parks a channel for documentID and returns it together with a
192	// removal function. The channel is closed on the next committed change to the
193	// document, or when the service stops.
194	func (s *Service) registerWait(documentID string) (ch chan struct{}, remove func()) {
195		ch = make(chan struct{}, 1)
196	
197		s.mu.Lock()
198		defer s.mu.Unlock()
199		if s.closed {
200			// Shutdown beat the registration: signal immediately so the caller does
201			// not park on a channel nobody will close.
202			close(ch)
203			return ch, func() {}
204		}
205		s.nextWait++
206		id := s.nextWait
207		set := s.waits[documentID]
208		if set == nil {
209			set = make(map[uint64]chan struct{})
210			s.waits[documentID] = set
211		}
212		set[id] = ch
213		return ch, func() {
214			s.mu.Lock()
215			if set, ok := s.waits[documentID]; ok {
216				delete(set, id)
217				if len(set) == 0 {
218					delete(s.waits, documentID)
219				}
220			}
221			s.mu.Unlock()
222		}
223	}
224	
225	// notifyWaiters signals every long poll parked on documentID and every
226	// subscription open on it. It is called only after a change-bearing
227	// transaction has committed, so parked readers observe the new rows when they
228	// re-query and pushed frames describe committed changes.
229	func (s *Service) notifyWaiters(documentID string) {
230		s.mu.Lock()
231		set := s.waits[documentID]
232		delete(s.waits, documentID)
233		s.mu.Unlock()
234		for _, ch := range set {
235			close(ch)
236		}
237		s.signalSubscribers(documentID)
238	}

1	// Package events is the change event service: the durable per-document change
2	// log together with everything written on top of it.
3	//
4	// Within a document every change has a client-supplied id. New ids receive a
5	// monotonically increasing cursor; re-posting an existing id is idempotent
6	// only when the deviceId and decoded JSON payload match, otherwise it is a
7	// conflict. Valid batches commit atomically in one serialized transaction, so
8	// cursors never repeat and no record is partially written, even under
9	// concurrent writers. Ordinary posts, offline replays, merges and snapshot
10	// restores all allocate from the same per-document contiguous cursor space.
11	//
12	// A document may also carry snapshots: caller-supplied JSON states pinned to
13	// existing change cursors. Snapshots are write-once per cursor — a matching
14	// re-post is idempotent, a differing one a conflict — and live apart from the
15	// change log. A restore appends an ordinary change whose payload is a
16	// snapshot's state, recording its provenance so a repeated restore after a
17	// restart keeps the same idempotency/conflict decisions.
18	//
19	// Reads page by cursor in ascending order. The session view and the document
20	// view are the same read; the HTTP layer adds the session/permission checks.
21	// Long polling and push subscriptions are in-memory observers of commits:
22	// they register before the confirming read, hold no durable state, and are
23	// woken only after a change-bearing transaction has committed.
24	//
25	// The service owns only its own tables. The registration and permission
26	// layers are reached through its Gate interface, so a replay or merge never
27	// reaches into another service's storage.
28	package events
29	
30	import (
31		"encoding/json"
32		"errors"
33		"fmt"
34	)
35	
36	// ErrStoreClosing reports that the service is shutting down and parked long
37	// polls have been woken so they can return without writing anything. The
38	// caller maps it to 503.
39	var ErrStoreClosing = errors.New("store is closing")
40	
41	// Change is one element of an inbound batch or one row of a listing.
42	type Change struct {
43		ID       string          // client-supplied change id, unique per document
44		DeviceID string          // originating device
45		Payload  json.RawMessage // decoded JSON value, stored verbatim
46	}
47	
48	// Result reports the outcome for one element of an accepted batch.
49	type Result struct {
50		ID      string `json:"id"`
51		Created bool   `json:"created"`
52		Cursor  int64  `json:"cursor"`
53	}
54	
55	// ListedChange is one row in a ListChanges response.
56	type ListedChange struct {
57		ID       string          `json:"id"`
58		DeviceID string          `json:"deviceId"`
59		Payload  json.RawMessage `json:"payload"`
60		Cursor   int64           `json:"cursor"`
61	}
62	
63	// MergeResult reports the outcome of an accepted MergeChange. Outcome is one
64	// of "idempotent", "applied" or "merged".
65	type MergeResult struct {
66		ID      string  `json:"id"`
67		Outcome string  `json:"outcome"`
68		Cursor  int64   `json:"cursor"`
69		Result  *Result `json:"result,omitempty"`
70	}
71	
72	// ErrConflict reports that a batch references an existing change id with a
73	// different deviceId or payload. The whole batch is rejected.
74	type ErrConflict struct {
75		ID string
76	}
77	
78	func (e *ErrConflict) Error() string {
79		return fmt.Sprintf("conflicting change %q for document", e.ID)
80	}
81	
82	// ErrStaleCursor reports that a merge targets a base cursor for an unknown
83	// document, or a base cursor greater than the document's current cursor. The
84	// caller maps it to 400; nothing is written.
85	var ErrStaleCursor = errors.New("baseCursor is unknown or ahead of the current cursor")
86	
87	// ErrSnapshotBase reports that a snapshot targets an unknown document or a
88	// cursor that is not an existing change cursor of the document. The caller
89	// maps it to 400; nothing is written.
90	var ErrSnapshotBase = errors.New("snapshot cursor is not an existing cursor of the document")
91	
92	// ErrCompactedBase reports that a merge targets a base cursor below the
93	// document's compaction boundary: the changes it would be checked against
94	// have left the online log, so the conflict check cannot be completed. The
95	// caller maps it to 400; nothing is written.
96	var ErrCompactedBase = errors.New("baseCursor is below the compaction boundary")
97	
98	// ErrSnapshotNotFound reports that no snapshot exists for the document and
99	// cursor. The caller maps it to 404.
100	var ErrSnapshotNotFound = errors.New("snapshot not found")
101	
102	// ErrSnapshotConflict reports that a snapshot already exists for the document
103	// and cursor with a different state. The stored snapshot is left unchanged.
104	type ErrSnapshotConflict struct {
105		Cursor int64
106	}
107	
108	func (e *ErrSnapshotConflict) Error() string {
109		return fmt.Sprintf("conflicting snapshot for cursor %d", e.Cursor)
110	}
111	
112	// ErrRestoreConflict reports that a restore references a change id that is
113	// already taken by an ordinary change, or by a prior restore whose deviceId,
114	// snapshot cursor or source state differs. Nothing is written; the caller maps
115	// it to 409.
116	type ErrRestoreConflict struct {
117		ID string
118	}
119	
120	func (e *ErrRestoreConflict) Error() string {
121		return fmt.Sprintf("change id %q conflicts with the change log", e.ID)
122	}
123	
124	// ExportedSnapshot is one row of an ExportSnapshots result.
125	type ExportedSnapshot struct {
126		Cursor int64           `json:"cursor"`
127		State  json.RawMessage `json:"state"`
128	}
129	
130	// RestoreResult reports the outcome of an accepted RestoreSnapshot.
131	type RestoreResult struct {
132		ID           string `json:"id"`
133		Created      bool   `json:"created"`
134		Cursor       int64  `json:"cursor"`
135		RestoredFrom int64  `json:"restoredFrom"`
136	}
137	
138	// schema is created when the service is constructed. Table and index shapes
139	// are unchanged from the pre-refactor layout, so data already on disk stays
140	// readable.
141	const schema = `
142	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS changes (
143		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
144		cursor      INTEGER NOT NULL,
145		id          TEXT NOT NULL,
146		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
147		payload     BLOB NOT NULL,
148		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, id)
149	);
150	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS changes_doc_cursor_idx
151		ON changes(document_id, cursor);
152	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS snapshots (
153		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
154		cursor      INTEGER NOT NULL,
155		state       BLOB NOT NULL,
156		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, cursor)
157	);
158	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS restores (
159		document_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
160		change_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
161		device_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
162		snapshot_cursor INTEGER NOT NULL,
163		change_cursor   INTEGER NOT NULL,
164		state           BLOB NOT NULL,
165		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, change_id)
166	);
167	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS restores_doc_cursor_idx
168		ON restores(document_id, change_cursor);
169	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS change_boundaries (
170		document_id TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
171		boundary    INTEGER NOT NULL
172	);
173	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS change_identities (
174		document_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
175		id            TEXT NOT NULL,
176		device_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
177		digest        BLOB NOT NULL,
178		cursor        INTEGER NOT NULL,
179		restored_from INTEGER,
180		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, id)
181	);
182	`

1	// Package authz is the permission service: the durable, per-document and
2	// per-device authorization ledger together with the system's single revoke
3	// verdict.
4	//
5	// Every (document, device) pair starts authorized; a grant or revoke is
6	// recorded per pair. The lookup and the write run in one serialized
7	// transaction on the shared connection and commit to disk, so concurrent
8	// grant/revoke calls each land as a complete state and survive a restart.
9	//
10	// The other services do not read the permission table. They take their
11	// registration-and-authorization verdict through AuthorizedTx, evaluated
12	// inside their own write transaction, so a rejected request is judged before
13	// any document content is observed and the gate and the gated work commit as
14	// one judgment. Revoking never deletes changes, snapshots, sessions or CRDT
15	// state; it only produces the denial and, after the revoke commits, notifies
16	// the registered revoke sinks (the live subscription registries) so they can
17	// end the affected connections with the one-time, sticky 4403 close.
18	package authz
19	
20	import (
21		"database/sql"
22		"errors"
23		"sync"
24	
25		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
26	)
27	
28	// schema is created when the service is constructed; its shape is unchanged
29	// from the pre-refactor layout, so authorization rows already on disk stay
30	// readable.
31	const schema = `
32	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS document_permissions (
33		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
34		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
35		authorized  INTEGER NOT NULL,
36		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, device_id)
37	);
38	`
39	
40	// RevokeSink observes a committed revoke. The change event service and the
41	// CRDT service register themselves to end the affected live subscriptions; a
42	// sink must not block and must be safe to call after the revoke transaction
43	// has committed. The permission service depends on this interface alone, so
44	// the dependency points from the observers toward the verdict and never back.
45	type RevokeSink interface {
46		PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID string)
47	}
48	
49	// Service is the permission service.
50	type Service struct {
51		db *sql.DB
52	
53		mu    sync.Mutex
54		sinks []RevokeSink
55	}
56	
57	// New constructs the permission service over the shared kernel handle and
58	// creates its table.
59	func New(kernel *store.Store) (*Service, error) {
60		db := kernel.DB()
61		if _, err := db.Exec(schema); err != nil {
62			return nil, err
63		}
64		return &Service{db: db}, nil
65	}
66	
67	// AddRevokeSink registers an observer notified after every committed revoke.
68	// It is called by the composition root while wiring the services, before the
69	// surface serves requests.
70	func (s *Service) AddRevokeSink(sink RevokeSink) {
71		s.mu.Lock()
72		s.sinks = append(s.sinks, sink)
73		s.mu.Unlock()
74	}
75	
76	// AuthorizedTx is the shared gate: it returns nil when deviceID is registered
77	// and currently authorized for documentID, store.ErrDeviceNotFound when the
78	// device is not registered and store.ErrPermissionDenied when its access has
79	// been revoked. It runs inside the caller's transaction q, so the verdict is
80	// taken on the same serialized connection as the work it guards, before any
81	// document content is read.
82	func (s *Service) AuthorizedTx(q store.DBTX, documentID, deviceID string) error {
83		exists, err := store.DeviceExistsTx(q, deviceID)
84		if err != nil {
85			return err
86		}
87		if !exists {
88			return store.ErrDeviceNotFound
89		}
90		var stored int
91		err = q.QueryRow(
92			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
93			documentID, deviceID,
94		).Scan(&stored)
95		switch {
96		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
97			// No deviation row: devices start authorized.
98			return nil
99		case err != nil:
100			return err
101		default:
102			if stored == 0 {
103				return store.ErrPermissionDenied
104			}
105			return nil
106		}
107	}
108	
109	// DeviceAuthorizedTx adapts the shared gate to the change event and CRDT
110	// services' Gate interface (which names *sql.Tx). The verdict is identical.
111	func (s *Service) DeviceAuthorizedTx(tx *sql.Tx, documentID, deviceID string) error {
112		return s.AuthorizedTx(tx, documentID, deviceID)
113	}
114	
115	// SetDocumentPermission grants or revokes deviceID's access to documentID and
116	// reports whether the stored permission actually changed.
117	//
118	// Every device starts authorized for every document, so the first revoke is
119	// the first write for the pair (changed=true); repeating a state that already
120	// holds writes nothing and reports changed=false. An unregistered device
121	// yields store.ErrDeviceNotFound and nothing is written. The lookup and the
122	// write run in one serialized transaction, so concurrent grant/revoke calls
123	// each commit completely and the final state matches the last committed
124	// action. After a revoke commits, every registered sink is notified; a grant
125	// notifies nothing (a prior revoke already ended the connection stickily).
126	func (s *Service) SetDocumentPermission(documentID, deviceID string, authorized bool) (changed bool, err error) {
127		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
128		if err != nil {
129			return false, err
130		}
131		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
132	
133		exists, err := store.DeviceExistsTx(tx, deviceID)
134		if err != nil {
135			return false, err
136		}
137		if !exists {
138			return false, store.ErrDeviceNotFound
139		}
140	
141		current := true // devices start authorized; a row only records a deviation
142		var stored int
143		err = tx.QueryRow(
144			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
145			documentID, deviceID,
146		).Scan(&stored)
147		switch {
148		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
149			// No row: the default (authorized) holds.
150		case err != nil:
151			return false, err
152		default:
153			current = stored != 0
154		}
155		if current == authorized {
156			return false, tx.Commit()
157		}
158	
159		v := 0
160		if authorized {
161			v = 1
162		}
163		if _, err := tx.Exec(
164			`INSERT INTO document_permissions (document_id, device_id, authorized) VALUES (?, ?, ?)
165			 ON CONFLICT (document_id, device_id) DO UPDATE SET authorized = excluded.authorized`,
166			documentID, deviceID, v,
167		); err != nil {
168			return false, err
169		}
170		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
171			return false, err
172		}
173	
174		// A grant cannot unblock a subscription (the first revoke already ended
175		// it, stickily); only a revoke needs to end live subscriptions.
176		if !authorized {
177			s.mu.Lock()
178			sinks := append([]RevokeSink(nil), s.sinks...)
179			s.mu.Unlock()
180			for _, sink := range sinks {
181				sink.PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID)
182			}
183		}
184		return true, nil
185	}
186	
187	// DeleteDevicePermissionsTx removes every document-permission ledger row that
188	// names deviceID, inside the caller's transaction: grants and revokes the
189	// deregistered device held on documents vanish together with the device. It is
190	// the permission service's share of device deregistration, run in the same
191	// serialized transaction as the registration layer's cascade, so the row
192	// removals and the device deletion commit as one judgment. After the device
193	// row is gone the default verdict would be "unregistered" anyway; clearing the
194	// rows guarantees a device that later re-registers the same id starts with no
195	// inherited authorization state.
196	func (s *Service) DeleteDevicePermissionsTx(q store.DBTX, deviceID string) error {
197		_, err := q.Exec(
198			`DELETE FROM document_permissions WHERE device_id = ?`, deviceID,
199		)
200		return err
201	}
202	
203	// DocumentAuthorized reports whether deviceID currently holds permission for
204	// documentID. Devices start authorized, so an absent row means authorized.
205	func (s *Service) DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID string) (bool, error) {
206		var stored int
207		err := s.db.QueryRow(
208			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
209			documentID, deviceID,
210		).Scan(&stored)
211		switch {
212		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
213			return true, nil
214		case err != nil:
215			return false, err
216		default:
217			return stored != 0, nil
218		}

221	// PermissionEntry is one row of a document's permission ledger: a currently
222	// registered device id together with its authorization for the document.
223	type PermissionEntry struct {
224		DeviceID   string
225		Authorized bool
226	}

228	// ListDocumentPermissions is the read-only ledger view of one document: one
229	// entry per currently registered device, in ascending lexicographic device-id
230	// order, paged by limit/offset against that same order.
231	//
232	// A device with no ledger row starts authorized, so its entry reports
233	// Authorized=true; a device whose latest committed action was a revoke reports
234	// false. Deregistered devices carry no device row and their ledger rows were
235	// removed by the deregistration cascade, so they never appear. An unknown
236	// document is indistinguishable from one on which every device keeps the
237	// default: every registered device lists authorized. The read runs in one
238	// serialized transaction, creates no row, moves no cursor and notifies no sink.
239	func (s *Service) ListDocumentPermissions(documentID string, limit, offset int64) ([]PermissionEntry, error) {
240		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
241		if err != nil {
242			return nil, err
243		}
244		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
245	
246		rows, err := tx.Query(
247			`SELECT d.id, COALESCE(p.authorized, 1) AS authorized
248			 FROM devices d
249			 LEFT JOIN document_permissions p
250			   ON p.document_id = ? AND p.device_id = d.id
251			 ORDER BY d.id ASC
252			 LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`,
253			documentID, limit, offset,
254		)
255		if err != nil {
256			return nil, err
257		}
258		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
259	
260		entries := make([]PermissionEntry, 0)
261		for rows.Next() {
262			var entry PermissionEntry
263			var stored int
264			if err := rows.Scan(&entry.DeviceID, &stored); err != nil {
265				return nil, err
266			}
267			entry.Authorized = stored != 0
268			entries = append(entries, entry)
269		}
270		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
271			return nil, err
272		}
273		return entries, tx.Commit()
274	}

1	// Package crdt is the CRDT state service: an automatically mergeable state
2	// layer that sits beside the change event log and never touches it.
3	//
4	// A document's CRDT type is declared with its first operation batch —
5	// "counter", "gset", "register" or "orset" — and never changes afterward; two
6	// batches declaring different types concurrently serialize in one transaction
7	// on the shared connection and exactly one takes effect.
8	//
9	// A counter carries each device's accumulated contribution; contributions
10	// only move forward and the merge is the sum of per-device maxima. A gset
11	// adds strings; the merge is the sorted union. A register carries an arbitrary
12	// JSON value and a strictly increasing per-device version; the merge is the
13	// greatest version, ties broken by the smaller operation id. An orset tags
14	// each add with its operation id and a remove tombstones only the adds it has
15	// observed, so concurrent removes never delete later adds; the merge is the
16	// sorted set of elements with a live tag. Every merge is commutative,
17	// associative and idempotent, so any reader converges to the same value.
18	//
19	// Operation ids are stable and unique per document; a repeat with the same
20	// device and comparison content is idempotent, any other repeat a conflict.
21	// Compaction trims rows that no longer participate in a merge while keeping
22	// one fixed-size identity digest per trimmed id, so idempotency and conflict
23	// decisions are unchanged afterward.
24	//
25	// The service owns only its own tables. Registration and authorization are
26	// reached through its Gate interface inside the write transaction, and
27	// committed state changes are published to in-memory state subscriptions. It
28	// never writes change rows, allocates cursors or reads another service's
29	// storage.
30	package crdt
31	
32	import (
33		"database/sql"
34		"encoding/json"
35		"errors"
36		"fmt"
37	)
38	
39	// CRDT document types.
40	const (
41		// TypeCounter is the grow-only counter: the merged value is the sum of
42		// each device's maximum accumulated contribution.
43		TypeCounter = "counter"
44		// TypeGSet is the grow-only set: the merged value is the union of all
45		// added elements.
46		TypeGSet = "gset"
47		// TypeRegister is the last-writer-wins register: the merged value is the
48		// value of the operation with the greatest version, ties broken by the
49		// lexicographically smaller operation id.
50		TypeRegister = "register"
51		// TypeORSet is the observed-remove set: the merged value is the set of
52		// elements with at least one add not tombstoned by an observed remove.
53		TypeORSet = "orset"
54	)
55	
56	// OR-Set operation actions.
57	const (
58		// ORSetAdd adds the operation's element with a fresh tag.
59		ORSetAdd = "add"
60		// ORSetRemove tombstones every add tag for the element that the operation
61		// observes.
62		ORSetRemove = "remove"
63	)
64	
65	// ErrNotFound reports that no CRDT operation has ever been committed for the
66	// document, so it has neither a type nor a merged state yet. The caller maps
67	// it to 404.
68	var ErrNotFound = errors.New("crdt state not found")
69	
70	// ErrConflict reports a rejected CRDT batch: the document's type is already
71	// fixed to another type, a counter contribution regressed, or an operation id
72	// already exists with different content or origin. Nothing is written; the
73	// caller maps it to 409.
74	type ErrConflict struct {
75		// ID is the conflicting operation id when one is known; it is empty for a
76		// document-level conflict (a mismatched declared type).
77		ID string
78		// Reason carries a short, machine-facing description of the conflict.
79		Reason string
80	}
81	
82	func (e *ErrConflict) Error() string {
83		if e.ID != "" {
84			return fmt.Sprintf("crdt conflict for operation %q: %s", e.ID, e.Reason)
85		}
86		return "crdt conflict: " + e.Reason
87	}
88	
89	// Op is one element of an inbound CRDT batch.
90	//
91	// For a counter, Value is the device's accumulated contribution: it must be a
92	// JSON number that is a non-negative integer, and it may never decrease for
93	// the same device. Elements and Version are unused.
94	//
95	// For a gset, Elements lists the strings the operation adds to the set and
96	// must be non-empty; Value and Version are unused.
97	//
98	// For a register, Value is an arbitrary JSON value stored verbatim and
99	// Version is a non-negative integer that must be strictly greater than every
100	// version the same device has already had accepted. Elements is unused.
101	//
102	// For an orset, Action is "add" or "remove" and Element is the non-empty
103	// string the operation adds or removes. Value, Elements and Version are
104	// unused.
105	type Op struct {
106		ID       string          // client-supplied stable id, unique per document
107		DeviceID string          // originating device (shared by the whole batch)
108		Value    json.RawMessage // counter: accumulated contribution; register: the value
109		Elements []string        // gset: elements to add
110		Version  int64           // register: logical version, per-device strictly increasing
111		Action   string          // orset: ORSetAdd or ORSetRemove
112		Element  string          // orset: the element the action applies to
113	}
114	
115	// State is a document's merged CRDT state.
116	//
117	// Value holds the type-specific merged result: for a counter it decodes to the
118	// JSON integer sum of per-device maxima; for a gset it decodes to the sorted
119	// JSON array of every accepted element (an empty set is []); for a register it
120	// is the winning operation's JSON value, exactly as submitted; for an orset it
121	// decodes to the sorted JSON array of the elements with at least one live add
122	// (an empty set is []).
123	type State struct {
124		Type  string          `json:"type"`
125		Value json.RawMessage `json:"value"`
126	}
127	
128	// Result reports the outcome for one element of an accepted CRDT batch.
129	type Result struct {
130		ID      string `json:"id"`
131		Created bool   `json:"created"`
132	}
133	
134	// Snapshot is a document's merged CRDT state together with the storage
135	// footprint of that state: Operations counts the stored operations the merge
136	// is derived from (counter and gset: rows of the operation log; register: the
137	// retained per-device operations; orset: the add tags, live or tombstoned)
138	// and Tombstones counts the stored orset tombstones (always zero for the
139	// other types). Both counts are non-negative; compaction drives them down to
140	// the operations and tombstones that still participate in the merge.
141	type Snapshot struct {
142		Type       string          // the document's fixed CRDT type
143		Value      json.RawMessage // the merged value, exactly as GetState derives it
144		Operations int64           // stored operations the merge is derived from
145		Tombstones int64           // stored orset tombstones; 0 for counter, gset and register
146	}
147	
148	// Gate is the only seam the CRDT service uses to reach the registration and
149	// permission layers. It is evaluated inside the write transaction, so a
150	// rejected submission is judged before any CRDT content is observed.
151	type Gate interface {
152		// DeviceAuthorizedTx returns nil when the device is registered and
153		// authorized, store.ErrDeviceNotFound for an unregistered device and
154		// store.ErrPermissionDenied after a revoke.
155		DeviceAuthorizedTx(tx *sql.Tx, documentID, deviceID string) error
156	}
157	
158	// schema is created when the service is constructed. Table shapes are
159	// unchanged from the pre-refactor layout, so CRDT data already on disk stays
160	// readable after the split.
161	const schema = `
162	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_documents (
163		document_id TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
164		type        TEXT NOT NULL
165	);
166	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_ops (
167		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
168		id          TEXT NOT NULL,
169		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
170		value       BLOB,
171		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, id)
172	);
173	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_counter_values (
174		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
175		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
176		value       INTEGER NOT NULL,
177		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, device_id)
178	);
179	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_set_elements (
180		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
181		element     TEXT NOT NULL,
182		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, element)
183	);
184	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_register_ops (
185		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
186		id          TEXT NOT NULL,
187		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
188		version     INTEGER NOT NULL,
189		value       BLOB NOT NULL,
190		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, id)
191	);
192	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_orset_tags (
193		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
194		element     TEXT NOT NULL,
195		op_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
196		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, element, op_id)
197	);
198	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_orset_tombstones (
199		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
200		element     TEXT NOT NULL,
201		op_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
202		removed_by  TEXT NOT NULL,
203		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, element, op_id)
204	);
205	-- op_identities keeps, for each operation id whose merge row compaction
206	-- trimmed away, the only information idempotency and conflict decisions still
207	-- need: the originating device and a digest of the type-specific comparison
208	-- content. Compaction never trims this table; it does not participate in any
209	-- merge and holds a fixed-size digest rather than the operation payload.
210	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS crdt_op_identities (
211		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
212		id          TEXT NOT NULL,
213		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
214		digest      BLOB NOT NULL,
215		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, id)
216	);
217	`
